stories.title: ChatGPT’s Computer History tracks your clicks and keystrokes
stories.simple_summary: ChatGPT's computer program can now watch everything you click and type on your computer, then use that information to suggest things you might want to automate or tasks to finish for you.
stories.why_it_matters: If you use ChatGPT on your Mac computer, know that it's watching your activity — decide if you're comfortable with that before turning this feature on.

stories.title: Google reportedly taps AMD to design next-generation TPU — hybrid AI ASIC could integrate on-package CPU cores for reinforcement learning
stories.simple_summary: Google is working with another chip company (AMD) to design better computer chips specifically for running AI programs.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors and big tech companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Rogue AI aren’t science fiction anymore
stories.simple_summary: The headline mentions that AI systems can now act on their own in ways that might be risky, but the article excerpt doesn't give enough detail to explain what actually happened.
stories.why_it_matters: This is mainly an engineering and safety concern for people who build AI — if you just use AI tools like ChatGPT, this doesn't directly affect you.

stories.title: Colleges aim to ‘AI proof’ degrees with new majors
stories.simple_summary: Universities are creating new college degrees and classes designed to teach skills that AI can't easily replace.
stories.why_it_matters: If you have kids or grandkids thinking about college, it's worth knowing that colleges are trying to prepare students for a world where AI exists.

stories.title: People Horrified That They’ll Be Busted Now That Anthropic Is Watermarking AI Content
stories.simple_summary: A company called Anthropic is adding invisible markers to content that AI creates, so you can tell when something was made by AI instead of a person.
stories.why_it_matters: In the future, you may be able to identify when text or images are AI-made, which helps spot fake or misleading content.

stories.title: National Transport Infrastructure Company deploys AI-based adaptive traffic lights across Israel
stories.simple_summary: Israel is using AI to control traffic lights that adjust in real-time based on how much traffic is on the road.
stories.why_it_matters: This could eventually come to your city — smarter traffic lights that reduce traffic jams, though it's mainly useful for very busy cities.

stories.title: Used Booksellers Are Racking Up Huge Sales. They're Not Thrilled About the Likely Reason
stories.simple_summary: Used bookstores are selling way more books than usual, likely because people are buying books instead of reading AI-generated text online.
stories.why_it_matters: If you're a book lover or a small bookstore owner, this shows that people still value real books over AI content.

stories.title: Machine Learning COFFIES “Hears” Sunspots Before We Can See Them
stories.simple_summary: Scientists created an AI system that can detect sunspots using sound patterns before scientists can see them with regular telescopes.
stories.why_it_matters: This is purely a scientific and astronomy tool — it doesn't affect everyday life or your business.

stories.title: Home province of DeepSeek, Moonshot founders seeks to retain future AI talent
stories.simple_summary: A Chinese province is trying to attract talented AI developers and engineers to stay or move there.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly matters to investors in tech companies — nothing you need to act on.

stories.title: Woman claims her stepfather used Grok to transform childhood photo into explicit imagery
stories.simple_summary: A woman reported that someone used an AI tool to turn her childhood photo into inappropriate sexual images without permission.
stories.why_it_matters: This shows a serious problem: AI can be misused to create fake harmful images, and you should be careful about photos of yourself or family members online.

stories.title: Have a laugh at AI’s expense by roleplaying as a chatbot
stories.simple_summary: Someone created a website game where you can pretend to be an AI chatbot and write silly responses, just for fun.
stories.why_it_matters: This is purely entertainment — it doesn't affect you unless you enjoy playing silly online games.

stories.title: Anthropic shares more details about how Claude’s new watermarks will work
stories.simple_summary: Anthropic is explaining the technical details of how their invisible watermarks will work to identify AI-created text and whether editing can remove them.
stories.why_it_matters: This mostly interests people who study technology or security — for regular people, it just means future AI text will be easier to identify.
